title: Content Delivery Protocols: FLUTE
method: code read against every requirement of the FLUTE documents in the library's scope, every open change read as merged into main, nothing built or run for the verdicts

releases.U: Unprofiled FLUTE: RFC 3926 (FLUTE version 1), RFC 3450 (ALC), RFC 3451 (LCT), RFC 5052 and RFC 3695 (FEC), RFC 5053 and RFC 6330 (Raptor, RaptorQ), RFC 3738 (WEBRC)
releases.M: MBMS download: TS 26.346 V18.2.0 clause 7.2 and annex A
releases.L: MBMS Download Profile: TS 26.346 V18.2.0 annex L.4, followed by both MBMS download and MBS Object Distribution
releases.B: MBS Object Distribution: TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 6.2, with the Profiled FDT Schema of TS 26.346 V18.2.0 annex L.6

dependencies.what: the MBSTF (rt-mbs-transport-function) sends and the MBS Client (rt-mbs-client, its MBSTF Client) receives with this library under the MBS profile
the BM-SC (rt-mbms-bmsc) sends and the MBMS Client (rt-mbms-client) receives with this library under the MBMS download profile

tx.name: FLUTE sender (Transmitter and FDT writer), and the senders built on it
tx.builtAgainst: RFC 3926, RFC 3450 and RFC 3451; RFC 6726 for version 2; TS 26.346 and TS 26.517 at Release 18

rx.name: FLUTE receiver (Receiver, FDT parser and file reassembly), and the clients built on it

features.name: Sessions, objects and packets
features.summary: The TSI and TOI are carried and checked as ALC and LCT require; the receiver checks the sender address only when the session names its source, and never leaves a session it cannot process.

requirements.name: Transport Session Identifier

cases.what: Every packet carries the TSI in the LCT header, as a 16-bit half-word, with an extra 32-bit word when the TSI needs it.
The half-word flag is always set, so S=0 and H=0 is never sent.

cases.case: The same TSI for every packet of the session
cases.what: The TSI is fixed when the sender is created and used for every packet, the close-session packet included.

cases.case: TSI unique among the sender's sessions
cases.what: The TSI is the value the caller configures; the library does not choose or reuse one.

requirements.name: Demultiplexing on sender address and TSI

cases.what: A packet from an address other than the session source is discarded, then the TSI is matched.
When the caller names no source address, only the TSI is checked, so packets with the session TSI from any sender are processed together.
The LCT header is parsed and checked (version, header length, field presence, extension lengths); a packet that fails is discarded and logged.

cases.case: Leaving after repeated unparseable or foreign packets
cases.what: The receiver discards such packets one by one but never leaves the session, however many arrive.

requirements.name: Transport Object Identifier at the sender

cases.case: A TOI greater than 0 for each file
cases.what: Files get TOIs from a counter that starts at 1 and skips 0 when it wraps.
Every packet carries a 16-bit TOI; only the data-less close-session packet omits it, as RFC 3926 requires.

cases.case: The same TOI for all packets of an object
cases.what: Every packet of an object is built from that object's file entry and its TOI.

requirements.name: Transport Object Identifier at the receiver

cases.case: Packets associated with objects by TOI
cases.what: Received symbols are placed in the object kept under the packet's TOI.
A packet whose TOI no FDT entry describes and which carries no EXT_FTI is discarded.

requirements.name: Joining a session

cases.what: The receiver is created with the address, port, TSI and, optionally, the source of the session it joins.
The ALC header is parsed and the payload placed by its FEC Payload ID.

cases.case: Dropping from a session it cannot process
cases.what: A packet the receiver cannot process is discarded, but the receiver stays joined; it never drops from the session.

requirements.name: FDT Instances in sequence

cases.what: Only one FDT Instance is in flight at a time: a new instance replaces the one being sent, and a repeat of the same instance waits for it to finish.

noted: A new instance abandons the one in flight, restarting from its first symbol, so a table that changes faster than it can be sent never completes.

requirements.name: Telling versions apart

cases.case: Version taken from EXT_FDT and the session
cases.what: A receiver configured for one version refuses FDT packets carrying the other.

features.name: LCT header and extensions
features.summary: The default LCT header and the extensions FLUTE uses are written and parsed as required, with the 3GPP specialisations (zero 32-bit CCI, 16-bit TSI and TOI, no SCT or ERT) under the profiles.

requirements.name: Default LCT header at the sender

cases.what: The version field is 1 and the default header layout is used.
The header is built in a zeroed buffer and reserved bits are never set.
HDR_LEN counts the base header, CCI, TSI, TOI and the extensions in 32-bit words.
C is 0 and a 32-bit CCI word is written.

cases.case: SCT and ERT only with T and R
cases.what: T and R are never set and neither field is written.

requirements.name: Default LCT header at the receiver

cases.what: A packet whose LCT version is not 1 is refused; the default layout is walked with lengths validated against the packet.
Reserved bits are not tested.

cases.case: SCT and ERT present only with T and R
cases.what: The two words are stepped over exactly when their flags are set.

cases.case: CCI of any length C allows
cases.what: C=0 is read as the WEBRC short format; other lengths are refused.

noted: The Codepoint is read as the FEC Encoding ID, a mapping the session description is supposed to carry; this library does not generate or read session descriptions.

requirements.name: Close Session and Close Object flags at the sender

cases.case: A set on every packet after the first
cases.what: Once the session is closing, every packet carries A; a data-less packet carries it when nothing is left to send.

cases.case: B set on every packet of a closing object
cases.what: Once an object is marked closing, every later packet of it carries B.

requirements.name: Close Session and Close Object flags at the receiver

cases.what: Either flag is passed to the application through the close callback with the TOI.
A packet with no payload ends processing without being taken for an FDT packet.

requirements.name: Expected Residual Time

cases.case: R not set beyond the bound
cases.what: R is never set.

requirements.name: Header extensions at the receiver

cases.what: Every extension is walked and checked while the header is parsed, before the packet is used.
HEL is read for HET 0 to 127; HET 128 to 255 is one fixed word.
Both are recognised and their content ignored.

requirements.name: Header extensions at the sender

cases.what: EXT_FDT is one word and EXT_FTI four, with HEL 4.

requirements.name: Version 2 on ALC and LCT of RFC 5775 and RFC 5651

cases.what: A session set to version 2 writes 2 in the EXT_FDT version field.

cases.case: SCT and ERT fields not used
cases.what: Under version 2 the T and R flags add no header words and are never set by the sender.
Version 2 is refused under the MBMS and MBS profiles, which are defined on RFC 3926.

requirements.name: EXT_TIME and the version 2 extensions

cases.what: EXT_TIME is recognised and skipped.

requirements.name: LCT header for MBMS download

cases.what: C is 0 and the CCI word is zero.
Under the 3GPP profiles a TSI above 65535 is refused, so every data packet carries the 16-bit half-word (S=0, H=1).

cases.case: 16-bit TSI in the data-less Close Session packet
cases.what: That packet carries no TOI, which needs H=0, so its TSI is 32 bits (S=1, H=0).
cases.conflict: RFC 3926 section 3.1: ALC packets "with the Close Session (A) flag set to 1 (signaling the end of the session) and that contain no payload (carrying no information for any file or FDT) SHALL NOT carry the TOI". RFC 3451 section 5.1 gives the TSI field as "32*S + 16*H bits in length" and the TOI field as "32*O + 16*H bits in length", so with no TOI H is 0. TS 26.346 V18.2.0 clause 7.2.7: "The Transmission Session Identifier (TSI) field shall be of length 16 bits (S=0, H=1, 16 bits)."

cases.what: The TOI is a 16-bit half-word (O=0, H=1).
Only the FDT goes on TOI 0.

cases.case: T and R set to zero
cases.what: Neither flag is ever set.
HDR_LEN is the whole header, extensions included, in words.

cases.case: EXT_TIME carries the ERT if included
cases.what: EXT_TIME is never included.

noted: TS 26.346 annex A sets the A flag to zero at the server when a Schedule Description is present; the library knows of no Schedule Description and sets A only when its caller closes the session.

requirements.name: FLUTE extension headers for MBMS download

cases.what: Every TOI 0 packet carries EXT_FTI.
Under the 3GPP profiles content packets never carry EXT_FTI.
FDT Instances are never encoded and EXT_CENC is never sent.

requirements.name: Extension headers and timing in the MBMS Download Profile

cases.what: Every FDT packet carries EXT_FTI.
The OTI of files is carried in the FDT, never in their packets.
T, R and EXT_TIME are never sent.

requirements.name: Timing fields ignored by the UE

cases.what: The fields are stepped over and EXT_TIME skipped; none is used.

features.name: File Delivery Table
features.summary: The FDT carries what each profile requires and none of what the MBMS Download Profile excludes, but the extended schema lacks its schema-version namespace and delimiters, the profiled schema's Cache-Control and File-ETag are written and read in the extension namespaces, a changed description keeps its TOI, Content-MD5 covers the unencoded file, FDT-Instance Content-Type and Content-Encoding are not applied to files, and numbering starts from 1.

requirements.name: The FDT of a session

cases.what: Every file sent is added to the session's table before its first packet.

cases.case: Each entry with TOI and URI
cases.what: Every File element carries TOI and Content-Location.

cases.case: Every file described in at least one instance
cases.what: The table is published on change and on its repeat timer.

requirements.name: FDT Instances on TOI 0 at the sender

cases.what: Only the FDT is sent on TOI 0; files never get it.

cases.case: EXT_FDT on every FDT packet, version 1
cases.what: Every TOI 0 packet carries EXT_FDT with version 1 and the instance ID.
Every TOI 0 packet carries EXT_FTI.
Instance IDs count up and restart from 0 after 2^20-1.
The first FDT Instance of a session has ID 1.

requirements.name: FDT Instances on TOI 0 at the receiver

cases.what: TOI 0 packets are reassembled per FDT Instance ID; a new ID restarts reassembly.
An EXT_FDT with a version other than 1 is refused.

requirements.name: FDT Instance syntax at the sender

cases.what: Every instance carries Expires.

cases.case: TOI and Content-Location on every File
cases.what: Both are always written.

cases.case: Content-Length and Content-Type as HTTP defines them
cases.what: Content-Length is the length of the file before any encoding; Content-Type is written when known.
gzip and deflate are applied with the framing their names mean, and declared.
Content-MD5 is computed over the file before content encoding; HTTP/1.1 defines it over the entity-body as transferred, so an encoded file carries the digest of the wrong bytes.

requirements.name: FDT Instance syntax at the receiver

cases.what: Expires is read, and a File without TOI or Content-Location is refused.
Read, with Content-Length used as the transfer length only when no encoding is applied.

cases.case: Content-MD5 checked as HTTP defines it
cases.what: The digest is checked over the decoded file, so a sender that computes it over the encoded entity-body, as HTTP/1.1 defines it, has its encoded files rejected.

cases.case: FDT-Instance Content-Type and Content-Encoding applied to files
cases.what: Content-Type and Content-Encoding are read only on File elements; values a sender gives on the FDT-Instance for all its files are not applied.

requirements.name: Extensions to the FDT schema

cases.case: Per-file descriptors on File, common ones on FDT-Instance
cases.what: Per-file extensions (File-ETag, Cache-Control) are written on File; FEC defaults and schemaVersion on FDT-Instance.

requirements.name: FDT dynamics at the sender

cases.case: Expiry in the future at creation
cases.what: An expiry at or before the current time is refused; the sender sets it twice the repeat interval ahead.
A changed content location, type, expiry or entity tag replaces the description of an object already described, under the same TOI; only a change of content gets a new TOI.

noted: A repeat re-sends the serialised instance unchanged, Expires included, until the table changes; a long-unchanged table can therefore be repeated after its own expiry. Not observed in a run.

requirements.name: FDT expiry at the receiver

cases.what: The held instance is dropped once expired, and packets it described wait for a fresh one.

requirements.name: Sending the FDT reliably

cases.case: FDT sent before the file it describes
cases.what: The table is queued on TOI 0, which is sent before any file.
The FDT is re-sent on its own repeat timer.

cases.case: FEC protection for an FDT over one packet
cases.what: The FDT is always sent with Compact No-Code, whatever its length, so a lost packet loses the instance until the next repeat.
With WEBRC, FDT packets go to the base channel only, which every receiver joins.

requirements.name: FDT at a version 2 sender

cases.case: No reuse of a live FDT Instance ID
cases.what: After 2^20-1, the lowest ID whose instance has expired is reused; with none expired the sender refuses rather than reuse a live one.
The RFC 6726 namespace can be written, but choosing version 2 does not select it: the default is no namespace.
Content-Type is written whenever the caller sets one; it is not required outside the 3GPP profiles.
An encoded file always declares its encoding.

requirements.name: FDT at a version 2 receiver

cases.what: An expired instance is dropped and not used to interpret later packets.
The 32-bit Expires is placed in the era nearest the current time.

cases.case: Newer declaration of a Content-Location wins
cases.what: Of two files with one Content-Location, the one declared by the higher FDT Instance ID is kept.

cases.case: Reuse of a live FDT Instance ID treated as an error
cases.what: An instance arriving under the ID of a live one is not detected; its packets are ignored as belonging to an object already completed.

cases.case: FDT not decoded under an unsupported FEC scheme
cases.what: A packet naming a scheme the library does not implement is refused before its symbols are used.
Elements and attributes the parser does not know are passed over.

requirements.name: FDT data for MBMS download

cases.what: Under the MBMS download profile the FDT is written in the urn:IETF:metadata:2005:FLUTE:FDT namespace of clause 7.2.10.1.
Always written.
Content-Length always; a file without a content type is refused.

cases.case: FEC Encoding ID, maximum source block length, symbol length, scheme-specific information
cases.what: Written on the FDT-Instance, and on a File whose values differ; Raptor writes its Z, N and Al.

cases.case: Compact No-Code maximum source block length at most 65535
cases.what: A larger value is refused under the 3GPP profiles.

Never written, although clause 7.2.9 makes it mandatory FDT data and annex A requires it of the server. Neither scheme in use defines it as part of its Object Transmission Information, so it is unclear what value it should carry; the sender holds one but does not write it.

cases.case: Content-MD5 when several versions are expected
cases.what: Every file carries Content-MD5.

noted: Release 19 adds Repair-Start and Repair-Limit-Percentage to the FDT data that may or may not be included, for unicast repair; they are not written or read, and repair is judged on the 5G Broadcast and 5G MBS pages.

requirements.name: Extended FDT schema version

cases.what: The schemaVersion element is set to 4.

19.what: The schemaVersion element is set to 4, the Release 18 value; Release 19 requires 5.

cases.case: schemaVersion and delimiter elements of the schema version namespace
cases.what: schemaVersion is written without a prefix, in the FDT namespace, and no delimiter element is written; the listing takes both from the schema version namespace (sv:schemaVersion, sv:delimiter) and its sequences require the delimiters.

requirements.name: FDT at the MBMS UE

cases.what: The held instance is dropped once expired; packets it described wait for a fresh one.
The receiver supports one schema version and parses every instance with it, ignoring schemaVersion and delimiter content.
The receiver takes every file the FDT describes, so all files of any group are received.

noted: Clause 7.2 also defines FullFDT, the MBMS session identity, the decryption key URI and the FEC redundancy level of a file. The MBMS Download Profile excludes them from the sender's FDT and leaves their support optional at the receiver; the receiver does not read them.

requirements.name: FDT in the MBMS Download Profile, sender

cases.what: Content-Type on every File; FEC Encoding ID, maximum source block length, symbol length and Raptor scheme-specific information on the FDT-Instance.

cases.case: Content-Encoding other than gzip, FEC-OTI-FEC-Instance-ID and Group not used
cases.what: Other encodings are refused; the instance ID and Group are never written.

cases.case: Complete, FullFDT and MBMS-Session-Identity-Expiry not used
cases.what: Complete is written only outside the 3GPP profiles; the others never.

cases.case: Content-Location, TOI, Content-Length and Content-MD5 on every File
cases.what: All four always written.

cases.case: File-level Content-Type and FEC OTI only to override
cases.what: The FEC OTI is written on a File only when it differs from the FDT-Instance, but Content-Type is written on every File and never on the FDT-Instance, so it does not override anything.

cases.case: Transfer-Length, Decryption-KEY-URI, FEC-Redundancy-Level and MBMS-Session-Identity not carried
cases.what: Transfer-Length is written only outside the 3GPP profiles; the others never.

requirements.name: FDT in the MBMS Download Profile, receiver

cases.case: FEC OTI supported at both levels
cases.what: Read at the FDT-Instance level and overridden per File.

cases.case: Content-Type and Content-Encoding supported at both levels
cases.what: Read only on File elements. A sender that gives Content-Type on the FDT-Instance, where clause L.4.4 puts it unless a File overrides it, leaves every file without a content type here.
Read on the FDT-Instance.
Read when present.
Read and checked on the reassembled file.
Read.
Read.
Not read, so an object marked max-stale is treated as carrying no caching directive.
Delimiter elements are not read.

requirements.name: Annex A: FDT attributes at the MBMS client and server

cases.case: Content-Location, TOI, Expires, Complete at the client
cases.what: All read.

cases.case: Maximum source block length, symbol length, maximum number of encoding symbols at the client
cases.what: All read, at either level.
Read and decoded per scheme.

requirements.name: Profiled FDT Schema, sender

cases.what: Under the MBS profile the FDT is written in the urn:3GPP:metadata:2022:FLUTE:FDT namespace of clause L.6.1.
The MBS profile applies every restriction of the MBMS Download Profile listed above.
The schemaVersion element is set to 2.

19.what: The schemaVersion element is set to 2, the Release 18 value; Release 19 requires 3.

cases.what: Every FDT Instance carries Expires.

cases.case: Cache-Control as the profiled schema declares it
cases.what: Cache-Control is written as mbms2007:Cache-Control, in the 2007 extension namespace; the profiled schema declares it in its own namespace, so a receiver of the profiled schema does not find it. The document still validates, since the schema admits elements of other namespaces.

cases.case: File-ETag as the profiled schema declares it
cases.what: File-ETag is written as mbms2012:File-ETag; the profiled schema declares it as a plain attribute of File.

noted: Release 19 removes File@Expires from the profiled schema, with the sentence giving it precedence over FDT@Expires; the code still writes File@Expires when one is set, which the schema admits as an attribute it does not declare.

requirements.name: Profiled FDT Schema, receiver

cases.what: An FDT in the profiled namespace is parsed.
A File's own Expires is read, and an accessor gives it precedence over the FDT-Instance one.

cases.case: File-ETag of the profiled schema read
cases.what: File-ETag is looked for only in the 2012 extension namespace, so the plain attribute of the profiled schema is not found.

cases.case: Cache-Control of the profiled schema read
cases.what: Cache-Control is looked for only in the 2007 extension namespace, so the profiled element is not found.

features.name: FEC and blocking
features.summary: Compact No-Code, Raptor and RaptorQ are sent and received, and blocking follows the documents; the decoder ignores the block structure the sender signals, a packet can mix source blocks, a short last symbol in a multi-symbol packet is lost, and RaptorQ's payload ID and EXT_FTI use the wrong field widths.

requirements.name: FEC Payload ID at the sender

cases.case: An FEC Payload ID in every data packet
cases.what: Every packet with symbols starts its payload with the SBN and ESI of its first symbol.

cases.case: One FEC Encoding ID per object
cases.what: An object keeps the scheme it was created with for all its packets.

requirements.name: FEC Payload ID at the receiver

cases.case: Symbols placed by SBN and ESI
cases.what: Each symbol is placed by its source block number and encoding symbol ID, out-of-range values refused.

A payload holding several symbols is split into consecutive ESIs, but the remaining length is not reduced as it goes, so a short last symbol is taken as a full one: nothing is copied, yet it is marked received.

requirements.name: FEC Object Transmission Information at the sender

cases.case: OTI in band, in the FDT
cases.what: Encoding ID, maximum source block length, symbol length and the Raptor scheme-specific information are in the FDT.

cases.case: Same OTI in EXT_FTI and the FDT
cases.what: For Raptor and RaptorQ objects sent with EXT_FTI, the extension carries the Compact No-Code layout (maximum source block length) where the FDT carries Z, N and Al.

requirements.name: FEC Object Transmission Information at the receiver

cases.what: EXT_FTI is parsed on TOI 0 packets.

cases.case: EXT_FTI or the FDT for Compact No-Code files
cases.what: A file is started from its FDT entry, or from its packets' EXT_FTI when no entry has arrived.

cases.case: EXT_FTI for Raptor and RaptorQ files
cases.what: For these schemes EXT_FTI gives no maximum source block length, so an object started from EXT_FTI alone fails to partition and is never received.
Whichever source arrives first wins: an object started from its FDT entry ignores EXT_FTI, and one started from EXT_FTI keeps it.

requirements.name: Symbols and blocking at the sender

cases.case: Equal symbol length, last one shorter
cases.what: Every symbol has the encoding symbol length except the last of the object.
Compact No-Code objects are partitioned with the RFC 3926 / RFC 5052 algorithm.

requirements.name: Symbols and blocking at the receiver

cases.what: The receiver partitions with the same algorithm from the same OTI.

requirements.name: Compact No-Code FEC scheme (FEC Encoding ID 0)

cases.what: The default scheme: 16-bit SBN and ESI, source symbols only.
Every source block of an object gets its own SBN, so no mapping needs communicating.

requirements.name: Raptor FEC scheme (FEC Encoding ID 1)

cases.what: Raptor is selected by FEC Encoding ID 1, with a 16-bit SBN and 16-bit ESI.
Objects are partitioned with the Partition function, Z from the maximum source block length, one sub-block and Al of 1.

cases.case: A packet holds symbols of one source block, all source or all repair
cases.what: When the symbol length is under half the payload, one packet can take symbols from more than one source block, or source and repair symbols together, and is labelled with the first symbol's SBN and ESI only.
Source and repair symbols are generated by the RFC 5053 encoder.

cases.case: Decoding with the signalled block structure
cases.what: The receiver recomputes Z from the maximum source block length and forces one sub-block and Al of 1, overwriting the Z, N and Al the sender signals; an object partitioned otherwise is not recovered.

requirements.name: RaptorQ FEC scheme (FEC Encoding ID 6)

cases.what: RaptorQ is selected by FEC Encoding ID 6 outside the 3GPP profiles.
The payload ID is written and read as a 16-bit SBN and 16-bit ESI; RFC 6330 gives an 8-bit SBN and a 24-bit ESI.
EXT_FTI is written and read with a 48-bit transfer length and 16 reserved bits; RFC 6330 encodes a 40-bit transfer length and 8 reserved bits.
Split into consecutive ESIs, but a short last symbol is taken as a full one and not copied.

cases.case: Decoding with the signalled block structure
cases.what: As for Raptor, the signalled Z and N are overwritten by the receiver's own partitioning.

requirements.name: Other FEC schemes

cases.what: Not implemented; a packet or FDT naming it is refused.
Not implemented; refused like any scheme the library does not know.

requirements.name: FEC Encoding ID in the Codepoint

cases.case: Codepoint equal to the FEC Encoding ID
cases.what: The sender writes the scheme's FEC Encoding ID in the Codepoint and the receiver reads it from there.

requirements.name: FEC Payload ID for MBMS download

cases.what: Written and read as two 16-bit fields.
Raptor uses the same 16-bit SBN and 16-bit ESI.

requirements.name: FEC schemes at the MBMS UE

cases.what: Received and reassembled.
Received Raptor symbols are decoded once enough have arrived.
The decoder ignores the Z, N and Al the sender signals and recomputes the partitioning, so a block a sender partitioned otherwise is not recovered.

requirements.name: Blocking at the MBMS sender

cases.what: Compact No-Code objects are partitioned with that algorithm.
Raptor objects are partitioned with the Partition function.
The maximum source block length is capped so a sub-block stays under 256 KB, and a larger one refused.

requirements.name: FEC schemes in the MBMS Download Profile

cases.what: Supported.
Supported only for objects partitioned with one sub-block and the source block count this receiver derives; the signalled block structure is not used.
The sender offers both and refuses any other scheme under the 3GPP profiles.
As at the MBMS sender.

requirements.name: Annex A: blocking and symbol encoding

cases.case: Blocking algorithm at client and server
cases.what: Both sides partition with the FLUTE blocking algorithm.

cases.case: MBMS Forward Error Correction at the client
cases.what: Required at the client; the Raptor decoder does not use the signalled block structure.

features.name: Congestion control and channels
features.summary: WEBRC runs on both sides outside the 3GPP profiles, whose single channel at a single rate is kept; the WEBRC receiver is never fed the measurements it needs, so it never joins a wave channel, and would not leave one.

requirements.name: Multiple-rate congestion control at the sender

cases.what: WEBRC is implemented for sessions outside the 3GPP profiles.

cases.case: CCI in every packet, C fixed for the session
cases.what: Every packet carries the 32-bit short-format CCI: time slot index, channel number and sequence number.
Packets are spread over the base and active wave channels in proportion to their scheduled rates.
The schedule sets each channel's share of the packets, not its absolute rate; the aggregate follows the rate limit rather than the wave rates.

noted: Without the WEBRC line, a session outside the 3GPP profiles is sent on one channel with C=0 and no congestion control.

requirements.name: Multiple-rate congestion control at the receiver

cases.what: A receiver outside the 3GPP profiles is refused unless WEBRC is configured.

Loss events come from per-channel sequence numbers, but the receiver never reports the first base-channel packet, round-trip times or reception rates to the controller, so it never joins a wave channel.

requirements.name: WEBRC sender

cases.what: The 32-bit short format is used.
Parameters that would need more than 255 are refused.

cases.case: Wave rates fall by P per time slot
cases.what: Wave rates follow the exponential decay across slots.

requirements.name: WEBRC receiver

cases.what: The receiver joins the session's own group, the base channel, at start.

No join before the first base packet, during a loss event or a join in progress, at N waves, or when the target rate is too low; as wired, the first condition is never cleared, so the receiver never joins a wave.
The controller implements the slow-start exits, but the receiver never feeds it join delays or reception rates, so none can fire.
Wave channels are joined but never left; the leave function exists but nothing calls it.
The current time slot index carried in the CCI is not acted on, so no slot change leaves the lowest wave.
No timeout makes the receiver leave the session when reception goes far from normal.

requirements.name: WEBRC supported

cases.what: WEBRC is implemented for sessions outside the 3GPP profiles.

requirements.name: One channel at one rate

cases.case: No congestion control under the 3GPP profiles
cases.what: Under the 3GPP profiles the sender uses one channel and refuses to enable WEBRC; the receiver joins without it.
One destination, paced only by the configured rate limit.

requirements.name: Congestion control in the MBMS Download Profile

cases.what: As for MBMS download.

features.name: Content encoding
features.summary: gzip files are decoded; under the 3GPP profiles the sender does not encode, since the profile leaves no way to carry the transfer length.

requirements.name: Content encoding of FDT Instances at the sender

cases.case: EXT_CENC only with an encoded FDT
cases.what: FDT Instances are not content encoded and EXT_CENC is never sent.

requirements.name: Content encoding of FDT Instances at the receiver

cases.what: EXT_CENC is read; an encoding the library cannot decode is refused.
The encoding read from EXT_CENC is not applied to the FDT: zlib and deflate instances are refused, and a gzip instance reaches the XML parser undecoded.

requirements.name: gzip for files

cases.what: A file with Content-Encoding gzip is inflated after reception.

cases.case: Sizing a gzip file from a conformant sender
cases.what: The receiver needs the transfer length of an encoded file; it waits for EXT_FTI when the FDT lacks it, which a sender under the profile does not send.
cases.conflict: TS 26.346 V18.2.0 clause L.4.2: "The following FDT attribute, defined at both the FDT-Instance and File levels, may be carried in the FDT sent by the FLUTE sender, under either the File-Instance or File element, and shall be supported by the FLUTE receiver:" (Content-Encoding set to gzip). Clause L.4.4 lists Transfer-Length under "The following attributes shall not be carried in the FDT sent by the FLUTE sender:", and clause 7.2.8: "FLUTE packets carrying symbols of files (not FDT Instances) shall not include an EXT_FTI." Raised as 5G-MAG Standards issue 212.

noted: The sender does not content encode under the 3GPP profiles, which the profile permits ("may be carried"); a request to do so is refused.

requirements.name: Annex A: content encoding

cases.case: FDT Instances not encoded by the server
cases.what: Never encoded.
gzip is decoded.
